correctness.rationale: Since p congruent 7 mod36, exponent a=4 always gives 9|p-16, and for a in {0,1,2,3,5}, 4 or 9 cannot divide the remainder. Any nonsquarefree positive remainder has a prime-square divisor q^2 with q>=5 and q<=floor(sqrt(10^9)); gcd(36,q^2)=1 yields a unique progression index k mod q^2 by inverse 36. The checker marks only positive remainders >=q^2 and scans every k=0,...,27,777,777 (27,777,778 integers), all prime q<=31623. Independent newly executed full exact mask sieve reproduced precisely nine integer five-obstruction candidates and precisely two prime survivors; complete deterministic trial division and factorization confirmed exponent 6 for both. Their lower exponent obstructions are explicit and the all-k range is exhaustive within <=10^9; this does not depend on a heuristic cutoff or primality assumptions.
